title: Distribution-free improper learning of two unrestricted halfspaces
formal: Is there a uniform randomized learner that, for every distribution on \(\{0,1\}^{n}\) and every target equal to the intersection of two integer-weight halfspaces, outputs an efficiently evaluable hypothesis of error at most \(\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(2/3\) in time polynomial in n, a supplied target-length bound B and \(1/\varepsilon\)?
definitions: A halfspace is \(h(x)=1\) exactly when \(\sum_{i} w_{i} x_{i}\ge \theta\), with \(w_{i},\theta \in Z\) in signed binary; equality is positive. The target f is the conjunction of two such predicates. Its description length is the bit length of a list of both weight vectors and thresholds, using self-delimiting binary integers. The learner receives n and B in unary and a rational \(\varepsilon\) with \(0<\varepsilon <1/2\) in binary. It is promised that f has at least one such description of length at most B, but receives neither that description nor its weights. An example oracle returns independent pairs \((x,f(x))\) with x sampled from an arbitrary fixed distribution D on \(\{0,1\}^{n}\). The learner receives only these labeled examples and its own independent fair coins. Each oracle call costs at least \(n+1\) steps to receive its bits; all further work is charged in Turing-machine bit steps. Membership queries, advice and descriptions or probability evaluations of D are absent. There must be a fixed polynomial P such that on every random tape the running time, and hence sample count and output length, are bounded by P(\(n+B+\lceil 1/\varepsilon \rceil +len(\varepsilon )\)). Output a deterministic Boolean circuit \(H:\{0,1\}^{n}\to \{0,1\}\) in the explicit \(\mathrm{AND}/\mathrm{OR}/\mathrm{NOT}\) basis. The success condition is \(\Pr _{\mathrm{examples}}\),coins\([\Pr _{x}\sim D[H(x)\ne f(x)]\le \varepsilon ]\ge 2/3\), uniformly over \(n,B,\varepsilon ,D\) and every promised f. Circuit evaluation costs polynomial time in its output encoding. The hypothesis need not be an intersection of halfspaces. Encoding an arbitrary deterministic polynomial-time evaluator by its Boolean circuit preserves this unrestricted efficient-output convention.

context_blocks.text: A single halfspace is efficiently learnable, but combining only two thresholds introduces a longstanding computational obstacle. Allowing an arbitrary output representation avoids the known hardness of proper learning.

The existing TCS-6544 explicitly assumes a positive margin and polynomial dependence on its reciprocal. This candidate instead concerns unrestricted integer-weight thresholds on the Boolean cube. The distinction affects the running time and cannot be hidden behind their similar titles.

why: Determine whether combining two elementary classifiers already defeats efficient distribution-free learning.
answer_criterion: Construct and analyze a learner satisfying all distribution, representation and polynomial-time quantifiers, or prove that no such learner exists. Proper-learning hardness or lower bounds for statistical-query algorithms alone do not rule out every learner in this model. A positive margin, Gaussian distribution or membership-query promise would change the target.
